cleanRule: Biology = explain the biological mechanism + link to evidence or data where provided + judge effectiveness/significance where directed
leaderboardTip: ~60% of HSC questions are Explain/Analyse/Evaluate type — show the biological mechanism (HOW and WHY), not just the outcome.

topics.title: Reproduction
topics.inquiry: How does reproduction ensure the continuity of a species?

dotPoints.label: 5-1a
dotPoints.text: Explain the mechanisms of reproduction that ensure the continuity of a species, by analysing sexual and asexual methods in a variety of organisms including animals (external/internal fertilisation), plants, fungi (budding, spores), bacteria (binary fission), protists (binary fission, budding)

dotPoints.label: 5-1b
dotPoints.text: Analyse the features of fertilisation, implantation and hormonal control of pregnancy and birth in mammals

dotPoints.label: 5-1c
dotPoints.text: Evaluate the impact of scientific knowledge on the manipulation of plant and animal reproduction in agriculture

topics.title: Cell Replication
topics.inquiry: How important is it for genetic material to be replicated exactly?

dotPoints.label: 5-2a
dotPoints.text: Model the processes involved in cell replication, including mitosis and meiosis, and DNA replication using the Watson and Crick DNA model including nucleotide composition, pairing and bonding

dotPoints.label: 5-2b
dotPoints.text: Assess the effect of the cell replication processes on the continuity of species

dotPoints.label: 5-3a
dotPoints.text: Construct appropriate representations to model and compare the forms in which DNA exists in eukaryotes and prokaryotes

dotPoints.label: 5-3b
dotPoints.text: Model the process of polypeptide synthesis including transcription and translation, assessing the importance of mRNA and tRNA, analysing the function and importance of polypeptide synthesis, and assessing how genes and environment affect phenotypic expression

dotPoints.label: 5-3c
dotPoints.text: Investigate the structure and function of proteins in living things

topics.title: Genetic Variation
topics.inquiry: How can the genetic similarities and differences within and between species be compared?

dotPoints.label: 5-4a
dotPoints.text: Conduct practical investigations to predict variations in the genotype of offspring by modelling meiosis, including crossing over of homologous chromosomes, fertilisation and mutations

dotPoints.label: 5-4b
dotPoints.text: Model the formation of new combinations of genotypes produced during meiosis, including autosomal, sex-linkage, co-dominance, incomplete dominance and multiple alleles; construct and interpret pedigrees and Punnett squares

dotPoints.label: 5-4c
dotPoints.text: Collect, record and present data to represent frequencies of characteristics in a population, including examining frequency data and analysing single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)

topics.title: Inheritance Patterns in a Population
topics.inquiry: Can population genetic patterns be predicted with any accuracy?

dotPoints.label: 5-5a
dotPoints.text: Investigate the use of technologies to determine inheritance patterns in a population, including DNA sequencing and profiling

dotPoints.label: 5-5b
dotPoints.text: Investigate the use of data analysis from large-scale collaborative projects to identify trends, patterns and relationships, for example population genetics in conservation management, determining inheritance of disease/disorder, and human evolution

topics.title: Mutation
topics.inquiry: How does mutation introduce new alleles into a population?

dotPoints.label: 6-1a
dotPoints.text: Explain how a range of mutagens operate including electromagnetic radiation sources, chemicals and naturally occurring mutagens

dotPoints.label: 6-1b
dotPoints.text: Compare the causes, processes and effects of different types of mutation including point mutation and chromosomal mutation

dotPoints.label: 6-1c
dotPoints.text: Distinguish between somatic mutations and germ-line mutations and their effect on an organism

dotPoints.label: 6-1d
dotPoints.text: Assess the significance of coding and non-coding DNA segments in the process of mutation

dotPoints.label: 6-1e
dotPoints.text: Evaluate the effect of mutation, gene flow and genetic drift on the gene pool of populations

topics.title: Biotechnology
topics.inquiry: How do genetic techniques affect Earth's biodiversity?

dotPoints.label: 6-2a
dotPoints.text: Investigate the uses and applications of biotechnology (past, present and future), including analysing social implications and ethical uses, researching future directions, evaluating potential benefits for society, and evaluating changes to Earth's biodiversity

topics.title: Genetic Technologies
topics.inquiry: Does artificial manipulation of DNA have the potential to change populations forever?

dotPoints.label: 6-3a
dotPoints.text: Investigate the uses and advantages of current genetic technologies that induce genetic change

dotPoints.label: 6-3b
dotPoints.text: Compare the processes and outcomes of reproductive technologies including artificial insemination and artificial pollination

dotPoints.label: 6-3c
dotPoints.text: Investigate and assess the effectiveness of cloning including whole organism cloning and gene cloning

dotPoints.label: 6-3d
dotPoints.text: Describe techniques and applications used in recombinant DNA technology, for example the development of transgenic organisms in agricultural and medical applications

dotPoints.label: 6-3e
dotPoints.text: Evaluate the benefits of using genetic technologies in agricultural, medical and industrial applications, and the effect on biodiversity of using biotechnology in agriculture

dotPoints.label: 7-1a
dotPoints.text: Describe a variety of infectious diseases caused by pathogens including microorganisms, macroorganisms and non-cellular pathogens; investigate transmission including direct contact, indirect contact and vector transmission

dotPoints.label: 7-1b
dotPoints.text: Investigate the work of Robert Koch and Louis Pasteur to explain the causes and transmission of infectious diseases, including Koch's postulates and Pasteur's experiments on microbial contamination

dotPoints.label: 7-1c
dotPoints.text: Assess the causes and effects of diseases on agricultural production including plant and animal diseases

dotPoints.label: 7-1d
dotPoints.text: Compare the adaptations of different pathogens that facilitate their entry into and transmission between hosts

topics.title: Responses to Pathogens
topics.inquiry: How does a plant or animal respond to infection?

dotPoints.label: 7-2a
dotPoints.text: Investigate the response of a named Australian plant to a named pathogen through practical and/or secondary-sourced investigation

dotPoints.label: 7-2b
dotPoints.text: Analyse responses to the presence of pathogens by assessing the physical and chemical changes that occur in the host animal's cells and tissues

topics.title: Immunity
topics.inquiry: How does the human immune system respond to exposure to a pathogen?

dotPoints.label: 7-3a
dotPoints.text: Investigate and model the innate and adaptive immune systems in the human body

dotPoints.label: 7-3b
dotPoints.text: Explain how the immune system responds after primary exposure to a pathogen, including innate and acquired immunity

topics.title: Prevention, Treatment and Control
topics.inquiry: How can the spread of infectious diseases be controlled?

dotPoints.label: 7-4a
dotPoints.text: Investigate and analyse the wide range of interrelated factors involved in limiting local, regional and global spread of a named infectious disease; investigate hygiene practices, quarantine, vaccination (passive and active immunity), public health campaigns, use of pesticides, genetic engineering

dotPoints.label: 7-4b
dotPoints.text: Investigate and assess the effectiveness of pharmaceuticals as treatment strategies for the control of infectious disease, including antivirals and antibiotics

dotPoints.label: 7-4c
dotPoints.text: Investigate and evaluate environmental management and quarantine methods used to control an epidemic or pandemic

dotPoints.label: 7-4d
dotPoints.text: Interpret data relating to the incidence and prevalence of infectious disease in populations; evaluate historical, culturally diverse and current strategies to predict and control the spread of disease

topics.title: Homeostasis
topics.inquiry: How is an organism's internal environment maintained in response to a changing external environment?

dotPoints.label: 8-1a
dotPoints.text: Construct and interpret negative feedback loops that show homeostasis using a range of sources, including temperature and glucose regulation

dotPoints.label: 8-1b
dotPoints.text: Investigate mechanisms used by organisms to maintain their internal environment within tolerance limits, including behavioural, structural and physiological adaptations in endotherms, hormones and neural pathways, and mechanisms in plants that allow water balance to be maintained

topics.title: Causes and Effects of Non-Infectious Disease
topics.inquiry: Do non-infectious diseases cause more deaths than infectious diseases?

dotPoints.label: 8-2a
dotPoints.text: Investigate the causes and effects of non-infectious diseases in humans, including genetic diseases, diseases caused by environmental exposure, nutritional diseases and cancer

dotPoints.label: 8-2b
dotPoints.text: Collect and represent data to show the incidence, prevalence and mortality rates of non-infectious diseases, for example nutritional diseases and diseases caused by environmental exposure

dotPoints.label: 8-3a
dotPoints.text: Analyse patterns of non-infectious diseases in populations including their incidence and prevalence

dotPoints.label: 8-3b
dotPoints.text: Investigate the treatment/management and possible future directions for further research of a non-infectious disease

dotPoints.label: 8-3c
dotPoints.text: Evaluate the method used in an example of an epidemiological study and evaluate the benefits of engaging in an epidemiological study

topics.title: Prevention of Non-Infectious Disease
topics.inquiry: How can non-infectious diseases be prevented?

dotPoints.label: 8-4a
dotPoints.text: Use secondary sources to evaluate the effectiveness of current disease-prevention methods and develop strategies for prevention of a non-infectious disease, including educational programs and campaigns, and genetic engineering

topics.title: Technologies and Disorders
topics.inquiry: How can technologies be used to assist people who experience disorders?

dotPoints.label: 8-5a
dotPoints.text: Explain a range of causes of disorders by investigating the structures and functions of the relevant organs, for example hearing loss, visual disorders and loss of kidney function

dotPoints.label: 8-5b
dotPoints.text: Investigate technologies that are used to assist with the effects of a disorder, including cochlear implants, bone conduction implants, hearing aids, spectacles, laser surgery and dialysis

dotPoints.label: 8-5c
dotPoints.text: Evaluate the effectiveness of a technology used to manage and assist with the effects of a disorder

Band6.descriptor: Demonstrates extensive knowledge and understanding of scientific concepts, including complex and abstract ideas. Communicates scientific understanding succinctly and consistently using correct and precise scientific terms in a variety of formats and contexts. Designs investigations to obtain accurate, reliable and valid data, evaluating and mitigating risks and making modifications in response to evidence. Selects, processes, interprets and represents qualitative and quantitative data to derive trends, show patterns and relationships, explain phenomena and make predictions. Designs solutions to scientific problems or hypotheses using primary and secondary data and scientific evidence. Applies knowledge and information to unfamiliar situations to propose comprehensive solutions or explanations for scientific issues or scenarios.
keyFeatures: Extensive knowledge including complex and abstract biological concepts
Precise and consistent scientific terminology throughout
Accurate, reliable and valid investigation design with risk evaluation
Data used to derive trends, patterns, relationships, explain phenomena and make predictions
Solutions designed using primary and secondary evidence
Comprehensive solutions applied to unfamiliar situations

Band5.descriptor: Demonstrates thorough knowledge and understanding of scientific concepts, including complex and abstract ideas. Communicates scientific understanding logically and effectively using correct scientific terms in a variety of formats and contexts. Designs investigations to obtain reliable and valid data, evaluating and mitigating risks and making some modifications in response to evidence. Selects, processes, interprets and represents qualitative and quantitative data to derive trends, show patterns and relationships. Designs solutions to scientific problems or hypotheses using primary and secondary data and scientific evidence. Applies knowledge and information to unfamiliar situations to propose explanations for scientific issues or scenarios.
keyFeatures: Thorough knowledge including complex and abstract biological concepts
Logical and effective use of correct scientific terms
Reliable and valid investigation design with some modifications
Data used to derive trends, patterns and relationships
Solutions proposed for unfamiliar situations with explanation

Band4.descriptor: Demonstrates sound knowledge and understanding of scientific concepts. Communicates scientific understanding effectively using scientific terms. Designs and plans investigations to obtain data, and evaluates risks. Processes, interprets and represents data using a range of scientific formats. Identifies scientific problems, questions or hypotheses and applies processes to primary or secondary data. Applies knowledge and information relevant to scientific issues or scenarios.
keyFeatures: Sound knowledge of biological concepts
Effective use of scientific terms
Investigation planning with risk evaluation
Data processed and represented in scientific formats
Knowledge applied to relevant scenarios

Band3.descriptor: Demonstrates basic knowledge and understanding of scientific concepts. Communicates scientific understanding using basic scientific terms. Implements scientific processes to obtain data, and identifies risks. Processes primary or secondary data, and represents it using scientific formats. Responds to scientific problems, questions, or hypotheses. Recalls scientific knowledge and information.
keyFeatures: Basic knowledge of biological concepts
Basic scientific terms used
Simple data processing and representation
Responds to problems with recall of knowledge

Band2.descriptor: Demonstrates limited knowledge and understanding of scientific concepts. Communicates scientific understanding using limited scientific terms. Partially outlines investigations to obtain data and information. Provides simple descriptions of scientific phenomena. Recalls basic scientific knowledge and information.
keyFeatures: Limited biological knowledge
Limited scientific terminology
Simple descriptions only
Basic recall

Band1.descriptor: Performance reported as Band 1 indicates that the minimum standard expected was not demonstrated.
keyFeatures: Minimum standard not demonstrated

dominant_question_types: Explain the mechanism of a biological process (e.g. explain how meiosis produces genetic variation)
Analyse data from investigations (e.g. analyse the results of a drug trial)
Evaluate the effectiveness of a technology or strategy (e.g. evaluate the effectiveness of vaccination programs)
Assess the significance of a discovery or process (e.g. assess the impact of recombinant DNA technology)
biology_specific_tips: Always name the specific biological molecule, cell type, or structure involved — not just 'the cell' or 'the system'.
Show the mechanism: state WHAT happens → explain HOW/WHY it happens → link to the biological outcome.
For evaluate/assess questions: weigh evidence on both sides, use quantitative data where available, then make a justified judgement.
Distinguish between correlation and causation when interpreting epidemiological data.
Use correct biological terminology consistently: mitosis vs meiosis, innate vs adaptive, pathogen vs disease.
common_errors: Confusing mitosis and meiosis — always specify which process and why it applies.
Describing immune responses without naming specific cell types (B cells, T cells, phagocytes).
Using 'it' or 'this' without a clear biological referent — always name the molecule, cell or structure.
Writing 'vaccines cause the body to fight disease' without explaining the mechanism (antigen → antibody → memory cell formation).
Forgetting to link homeostatic mechanisms back to maintaining the internal environment within tolerance limits.

explain_steps: Identify the biological process, structure or concept named in the question.
State the initial condition or stimulus.
Describe the mechanism step-by-step using correct biological terminology.
Link the mechanism to the biological outcome relevant to the question.
Use causal connectives (because, therefore, which causes, resulting in) to show reasoning.
evaluate_steps: Identify the subject of evaluation (technology, strategy, process).
Present evidence or reasoning supporting its effectiveness.
Present evidence or reasoning against or limiting its effectiveness.
Weigh the evidence using quantitative data or specific examples where possible.

before_output: Has the directive verb been answered correctly?
Has every part of the question been addressed?
Is the terminology specific (named cell types, molecules, structures)?
Are the causal links or mechanisms clearly explained?
Has stimulus data been used where provided?
Has a judgement been made when required (evaluate/assess)?
band6_checklist: Mechanism explained step-by-step with correct sequencing.
Named molecules, cell types and structures throughout.
Evidence, data or examples integrated into the response.
Response is coherent and logically sequenced.
Judgement is explicit and justified if required by the question.

target_band_selection_rule.Band6: Generate with extensive precision, named biological structures/molecules/cell types, step-by-step mechanism, integrated evidence and strong justified judgement. Succinct and consistently precise.
target_band_selection_rule.Band5: Generate with thorough, logically sound biological explanation and clear terminology. Slightly less integrated or precise than Band 6; applies to unfamiliar situations but with less comprehensiveness.
target_band_selection_rule.Band4: Generate with sound core biological content, effective use of scientific terms, and clear structure. Interprets data and applies knowledge to relevant scenarios, but with reduced mechanistic depth.
target_band_selection_rule.Band3: Generate basic, mostly descriptive responses using simple scientific terms. Recall facts and respond simply. Limited explanation and basic data processing only.
target_band_selection_rule.Band2: Generate very simple, partial and underdeveloped responses using minimal scientific language. Simple descriptions and basic recall only.
target_band_selection_rule.Band1: Do not intentionally generate unless explicitly requested as a wholly inadequate response example.

forbidden_behaviours: Do not generate Band 6 responses by merely increasing word count.
Do not use vague biological references — always name the specific structure or molecule.
Do not ignore the syllabus or stimulus.
Do not use vague judgements such as 'it is effective' without criteria or evidence.
